title: The Survey Slot
protagonist: Renee Okafor, telescope-time allocation scheduler, university robotic observatory exoplanet program
primary_metric: expected confirmed transit detections per hour of telescope time

options.A: The Candidate Watch -- commit the full 4-hour slot to re-observing one already-flagged transit candidate
options.B: The Twelve-Field Sweep -- split the slot across twelve independent fields searching for new, undetected transit signals

_ext: keys below are pipeline extensions, additive to SPEC §4

sources.claim: TESS Prime Mission TOI catalog false-positive rate
sources.title: The TESS Objects of Interest Catalog from the TESS Prime Mission
sources.note: Published in The Astronomical Journal, 2021. 74.8% non-false-positive rate is derived (1 - 565/2241) and applied to tonight's specific candidate as MA2, a modeling convention, not a claim that this exact candidate has this exact probability.

sources.value: 4034 candidates from roughly 200,000 target stars (a little over 2%)
sources.title: Planetary Candidates Observed by Kepler VIII: A Fully Automated Catalog With Measured Completeness and Reliability Based on Data Release 25
sources.note: Published in ApJS 235, 38. The paper states 4034 planet candidates and describes Kepler as observing approximately 200,000 stars overall (about 160,000 at a time) -- corrected 2026-09-18 after a P6 data-decay pass found the previously-recorded precise denominator of 189,516 does not appear anywhere in this paper (it likely came from a separate DR25 stellar-properties table, e.g. Mathur et al. 2017, which was never actually fetched or cited). Informs MA3's basis as a real per-star yield rate over a 4-year continuous baseline -- not a direct citation for the per-field, single-look rate this case needs, which is a disclosed assumption scaled from this real figure.

sources.title: The First Habitable Zone Earth-Sized Planet From TESS II: Spitzer Confirms TOI-700 d
sources.note: Used in Appendix E / Challenge D5 for scientific-to-standard-notation conversion.

sources.claim: Kepler-186f planet-to-star radius ratio, used to derive transit depth via depth = (Rp/Rs)^2
sources.title: Kepler-186f
sources.note: Corrected 2026-09-18 after a P6 data-decay pass found the previously-recorded value (~510 ppm) does not appear anywhere on this page as written -- the page states only the planet/star radius ratio (0.021). This case now derives the depth itself using the standard transit-depth relation depth=(Rp/Rs)^2 = 0.021^2 = 0.000441, shown as a derived value rather than a directly-quoted figure. Used in Appendix E / Challenge D5.

sources.claim: NASA Exoplanet Archive's Transiting Planets Table reports transit depth as a percentage (its own "Depth [%]" column)
sources.title: Data Column Definitions for Transiting Planets Table
sources.note: Corrected 2026-09-18 after a P6 data-decay pass found the archive's own documented column is 'Depth [%]' (percent), not 'ppm' as this case originally claimed -- no 'ppm' string appears on this page. Context only -- establishes that Appendix E's data is drawn from a real, live, student-explorable public data portal; the D5 scientific-notation exercise is grounded in how the source papers (S3, S4) actually report these specific planets' depths, not in the archive's own percent-based column format.

not_found: A real, published per-field detection probability for a hypothetical new 12-field shallow transit survey -- no completed survey publishes this exact figure for a single short look. Became MA3, informed by (not equal to) Kepler's real per-star yield rate (S2).

A real-time confirmation probability for any one specific, still-unconfirmed transit candidate -- no source publishes this for an individual candidate before follow-up occurs. Became MA2, applying the real population-level TESS rate (S1) to this case's fictional candidate as a disclosed modeling convention.

A specific observatory's specific nightly target list, analysis-team staffing, or same-night write-up capacity -- this is operational, program-specific data no observatory publishes for a single night. Became MA1, MA4, MA5.

A specific real transit candidate matching this case's exact fictional scenario (predicted transit window landing on a specific fictional night) -- the candidate in this case is a fictional composite, disclosed in scenario_constructions, grounded in the real TESS/Kepler vetting statistics (S1, S2) rather than naming one specific real, still-active candidate whose ephemeris would keep changing after this case is written.
scenario_constructions: Renee Okafor and the specific observatory in this case are fictional, invented for this case -- consistent with the corpus convention (e.g. Rosa Delgado / the Fermenter case, Marcus Feld / The Manifest Split).

The specific flagged transit candidate in The Candidate Watch is a fictional composite, not a named real TESS or Kepler object -- naming a real, still-active candidate would require freezing its ephemeris and follow-up status at an 'as of' date per SPEC §5's still-changing-entity rule, and no public source publishes a real-time confirmation probability for one specific unconfirmed candidate. The candidate's non-false-positive probability (MA2) is instead grounded in a real, cited population-level statistic (S1).

Tonight's exact slot parameters (4 hours, 12 fields, 5 flagged, 2 follow-up slots) and the 10% per-field detection rate (MA3) are constructed to create a genuine, close decision within SPEC §2's ~20% balance margin; they are not derived from any single real observatory's actual nightly log.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Tonight's slot length and field count
modeling_assumptions.basis: No public source publishes one specific observatory's specific nightly schedule. Set at a scale consistent with a real robotic survey program's typical single-slot allocation.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: The case's structure depends on this split, but the comparison method itself is not sensitive to the exact field count chosen.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Probability tonight's specific candidate confirms as a real detection
modeling_assumptions.basis: Applies Appendix A's real, published TESS Prime Mission population-level non-false-positive rate (S1) to this one fictional candidate, as a modeling convention -- no public source publishes a real-time confirmation probability for one specific, still-unconfirmed candidate.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Per-field probability of a new detection in a 20-minute shallow look
modeling_assumptions.basis: Informed by, but not equal to, Kepler DR25's real realized planet-candidate yield of ~2.1% per target star over a 4-year continuous baseline (S2). Set higher than the raw per-star figure to reflect thousands of stars per sweep field, but well below what a naive per-star scale-up would suggest, to reflect a 20-minute look versus 4 continuous years. No public source publishes a per-field rate for a hypothetical new shallow sweep directly.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Number of preliminary flags (pre-confirmation) in a given night's shallow pass
modeling_assumptions.basis: No public source publishes a specific sweep's preliminary-flag rate for a hypothetical new program. Set at a plausible fraction -- deliberately higher than Appendix C's ~1-2 expected confirmed detections per night -- consistent with a real automated significance test flagging more candidates than end up surviving the false-positive check, the same relationship Appendix A shows for TESS's own real catalog.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Changes the size of the D4 combination/permutation counts only, not the D1-D3 rate comparison.

modeling_assumptions.basis: Grounded in the real, general operational fact that a small on-call analysis team has a fixed number of working hours before a fixed morning-report deadline; no public source publishes an exact per-night write-up count for a specific program. Corrected 2026-09-18: an earlier version of this assumption used a 'downlink bandwidth' framing that a fresh P7 accessibility cold-read found operationally unpicturable for a ground-based observatory (real satellite-style downlink jargon applied to a facility with no stated satellite link) -- reframed to a plain staffing/deadline constraint, which needs no specialized astronomy infrastructure to picture.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Changes the size of the D4 combination/permutation counts only.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: How a confirmed detection is counted for D1/D3
modeling_assumptions.value: A night counts as producing one confirmed detection if at least one independent event succeeds; extra simultaneous successes are not double-counted
modeling_assumptions.basis: A stated counting convention, not a sourced figure. Renee's report to the committee is a yes/no ('did tonight's slot produce a new confirmed signal'), matching real observatory nightly-summary reporting practice, not a raw tally -- so 'at least one' is the quantity that matters for both options, and it is the only convention that puts The Candidate Watch (which can only ever produce one detection) and The Twelve-Field Sweep on the same footing. Added 2026-09-18 after a fresh P2 both-sides-solve pass found that, without this convention stated explicitly, a student could reasonably use the raw expected count (n times the per-field rate = 1.2) instead of D1's complement-rule answer (0.718) for the Sweep, which would silently change the entire balance test outcome (a ~60% Sweep win) without the case ever having said which convention it intends.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: This is a modeling convention, not a numeric dial -- it is not swept in sensitivity_model.py's FLEX[]. It is disclosed here because it is genuinely load-bearing to which formula D1/D3 use, even though it carries no numeric value of its own to flex.

sensitivity_note: No SPEC Section 6 subject-matter sensitivity applies. This is a scheduling/resource-allocation decision with no death, illness, or family-hardship stakes.

balance.argument_a: The Candidate Watch wins on tonight's actual numbers (4.22% margin) because a single already-flagged candidate's 74.8% confirmation chance, spread over the full 4-hour slot (0.187 confirmed detections/hour), edges out the Sweep's compound 'at least one of twelve' probability (0.179 confirmed detections/hour) -- and The Candidate Watch's rate is structurally simple: it depends on exactly one number, not twelve independent ones compounding together.
balance.argument_b: The Twelve-Field Sweep is not far behind (71.8% chance of at least one new detection across the slot) and carries an upside The Candidate Watch cannot: a hit is a brand-new discovery, not a confirmation of something already suspected, and the Sweep's per-field rate is the one number most likely to be conservative -- Appendix F's MA3 basis note explains it was set well below a naive scale-up of Kepler's real per-star yield, so the true rate plausibly runs higher than modeled.
balance.margin_basis: Compute rate_A = P(candidate confirms) / slot_hours using Appendix C's non-false-positive rate; compute rate_B = P(at least one of 12 independent fields detects) / slot_hours using the complement rule on Appendix C's per-field rate; compare the two rates.
balance.twist_effect: An archival cross-match (a real class of follow-up check used to rule out blended background objects, the same false-positive cause Appendix A already names) arrives mid-discussion: a faint background star is found nearly blended with the candidate's target star, and the probability the candidate survives the false-positive check drops from 74.8% to 55%. New rate_A = 0.55/4 = 0.1375 detections/hour, which is now BELOW rate_B (0.17939) -- the winner flips from The Candidate Watch (A) to The Twelve-Field Sweep (B), margin 30.47%. This twist deliberately changes the SAME quantity Appendix C/MA2 defines (the false-positive-survival probability), via a mechanism consistent with Appendix A's own named false-positive causes -- not a scheduling/timing change. Disclosed here and in sensitivity_model.py; never in case.md or FACILITATOR.md's student-facing sections.
balance.stability: Base margin (4.22%) is tight and a direct function of MA2 and MA3 via sensitivity_model.py. See sensitivity_disclosure[] -- MA3 flips the winner at +50% flex (within the 20% cap); MA2 flips the winner at -50% flex (breaching the cap). This is a real, disclosed finding about how tightly this case's already-close margin depends on two population-derived assumptions, not a defect.

sensitivity_disclosure.justification: MA2 applies a real cited population rate (S1) to one specific fictional candidate as a modeling convention -- the convention itself, not the underlying population statistic, is what's flexed. Flexing +50% is capped at 100% (the maximum a probability can reach): rate_A rises to 0.25, margin widens to 39.36% (breaches the 20% cap), no flip. Flexing -50% (to 37.4%) flips the winner to B, margin 91.89% (breaches the cap). This is the single most load-bearing assumption in the model.

MA3 has no citable per-field, per-look source; it is an irreducible scenario estimate scaled from a real per-star, multi-year statistic (S2). Flexing +50% (to 15%) flips the winner to B, margin 14.69% (within the 20% cap). Flexing -50% (to 5%) does not flip the winner but breaches the cap sharply (62.71%, A wins much wider).

deliverables.text: A compound-probability calculation for The Twelve-Field Sweep: the probability at least one of the twelve independent fields turns up a new detection tonight, via a probability tree or the complement rule.
A single-event probability statement for The Candidate Watch, using Appendix C's non-false-positive rate.
An expected-detections-per-hour comparison table for each option and the percent margin between them.

A write-up combinations-and-permutations plan: the number of possible preliminary-flag subsets the on-call team could write up (combination), and the number of possible orders for writing up a chosen subset (permutation).
A standard-notation data table converting Appendix E's real transit-depth figures, plus identifying which Appendix C columns are not needed for tonight's decision.

facilitator.twist: 40 minutes into the slot, an archival cross-match flags a faint background star nearly blended with the candidate's target star in older survey images -- the same kind of blended-object false-positive cause Appendix A already names -- dropping the probability it survives the false-positive check from 74.8% to 55% -- flipping the winner from The Candidate Watch to The Twelve-Field Sweep.

derived.notes: Computed by sensitivity_model.py; kept here so FACILITATOR.md's data walkthrough stays checkable against a value of record.
derived.html_meta_charset_artifact_note: The published HTML's <meta charset="utf-8"> declaration contains the digit 8, which T1-18's orphan-number sweep picks up as a bare number outside <script> (the same artifact the-manifest-split's case coincidentally avoided because its own real data happened to include the value 8). This entry documents that '8' as accounted for, not a real orphaned figure.

cohort_bands.note: Socratic plan runs as written in FACILITATOR.md. Anchor 1 vote is a real show-of-hands split worth reading; both deep-conflict threads run.

Combine Anchor 2 and Anchor 3 into one pass. Run only the sharper deep-conflict thread (the naive-multiplication trap and why it's wrong) at 20:00-30:00. Twist still drops at 15:00. Total runtime ~30 min.

No vote at Anchor 1 -- the learner states an initial position instead. The guide argues the other side directly rather than cold-calling. The twist still lands; 'who reverses' becomes 'would you reverse, and why'. Skip the deep-conflict threads; go straight from twist-recommit to Close.

tier2.P7: PASS (after 3 remediation rounds -- see QA_REPORT.md addendum)

qa_findings_resolved.finding: A subagent found Option B's D1/Appendix-C per-field rate read as a raw 'flag' while Option A's D2 rate is explicitly a 'confirmed' detection -- an apples-to-oranges comparison that would make D3's margin a paper number once a peer pressed on 'confirmed vs. flagged', especially since Appendix D implies most Sweep flags never get same-night follow-up at all.
qa_findings_resolved.fix: Reworded case.md Background/Appendix C/Appendix D (and the published HTML and FACILITATOR.md) so Appendix C's Sweep rate explicitly represents a genuinely CONFIRMED detection (same false-positive-survival standard as Option A), and Appendix D now governs a separate, downstream 'deeper characterization' capacity decision, not confirmation itself. D3's comparison is now apples-to-apples by construction.

qa_findings_resolved.finding: A subagent found the twist changed Appendix C/MA2's 'not a false positive' classification probability via an ephemeris/timing mechanism ('the transit might not happen in the window') that is a different random variable than the one Appendix A/C actually defines and sources -- a definitional mismatch a careful student could raise. A secondary, lower-stakes finding: the twist's '40 minutes into the slot' framing was never reconciled with Appendix B's fixed 4-hour rate denominator.
qa_findings_resolved.fix: Reworded the twist's mechanism (case.md is untouched -- the twist itself never lived there per SPEC -- but FACILITATOR.md, case.json, and the published HTML) to a background-object contamination alert, which is exactly the blended-object false-positive cause Appendix A already names, so the twist now changes the SAME quantity it always claimed to change. Added one sentence to case.md Appendix B stating per-hour rates always use the fixed nominal slot length, closing the secondary denominator ambiguity.

qa_findings_resolved.finding: A fresh subagent re-checking the earlier fix confirmed the confirmed-vs-flagged concern was resolved, but surfaced a deeper, previously-undisclosed issue: Challenge D3 asks students to use D1's 'at least one' compound probability as the Sweep's 'expected confirmed detections,' but the mathematically standard expected value of 12 independent Bernoulli trials is n*p = 1.2, not P(at least one) = 0.718 -- a materially different number that would flip the balance test outcome by a wide margin (~60% Sweep win) if a student used it instead, with the case never having stated which convention it intends.
qa_findings_resolved.fix: Added MA6 to case.md Appendix F (and case.json.modeling_assumptions): an explicit, disclosed counting convention stating that a night counts as producing one confirmed detection if at least one independent event succeeds (extra simultaneous successes not double-counted), justified by Renee's report to the committee being a yes/no rather than a raw tally, and by this being the only convention that puts a single-shot option (Candidate Watch) and a multi-trial option (Sweep) on the same footing. Background and Challenge 3/D1 now reference this convention explicitly.

qa_findings_resolved.finding: A fresh subagent, re-reading the corrected case.md, still could not concretely picture the Appendix D mechanism: 'downlink bandwidth' and 'battery' framing for a same-night characterization capacity limit reads as satellite-style jargon applied to a ground-based university observatory with no stated satellite link, leaving the actual physical process (what gets transmitted, where, why 'before dawn') unpicturable despite every individual word being familiar.
qa_findings_resolved.fix: Replaced the downlink/battery framing throughout (case.md Background/Appendix D/Appendix F/MA5, case.json, and the published HTML) with a plain staffing/deadline constraint: a small on-call analysis team can only fully write up and cross-check a limited number of confirmed detections before a fixed morning-report deadline. This requires no specialized astronomy infrastructure to picture and uses only ordinary workplace-deadline vocabulary.
